Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM` calls `doTest` with the path "b:foo/test" expecting the path "/b:foo[1]/test[1]". The current bug report indicates a severe problem: requesting `.asPath()` on a node causes an endless loop when the default namespace is reset (XML nodes with empty namespaces mixed with prefixed namespaces). Examining the `NodePointer.asPath()` method shows a recursion pattern where if the parent is a container, the parent is responsible for appending this node's path part, so it returns `parent.asPath()`. Otherwise, it recursively appends the parent's path and then appends its own node name. 

The method `isContainer()` always returns false in `NodePointer`, but there is a derived class `ContainerPointer` which overrides `asPath()` to return just the parent path or root. This setup means that if the parent is a container, the child's `.asPath()` method depends solely on the container's `.asPath()`. 

The infinite loop likely occurs because when the default namespace is reset on an inner element (empty namespace), `asPath()` repeatedly calls itself on parent nodes without ever progressing due to a cycle between `NodePointer.asPath()` and `ContainerPointer.asPath()`. The `ContainerPointer.asPath()` simply returns `parent.asPath()`, and if the parent is the original node or another container that calls back, this causes endless recursion.

The core cause is the missing or broken handling of nodes with empty namespaces in `asPath()` navigation logic, which causes the path building recursion to never terminate and loop infinitely when default namespace resets cause certain nodes to appear as containers improperly or the `isContainer()` method does not properly identify container nodes to break the recursion chain correctly. 

This explains the failure in the test and the problem described in the bug report—resetting the default namespace causes `.asPath()` to loop infinitely.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
